# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1727
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1727
- **Title**: feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 net→emit→render timing trail
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/stream-trace` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +461
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T19:23:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T20:48:59Z

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

- **State**: open

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

# pr-1727: feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 net→emit→render timing trail

## Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

    "description": "## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)

- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate"

{
  "key": "pr-1727",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 net→emit→render timing trail",
    "description": "## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`

1. **Double emit marks via wrapper streams** (dial, silent_stream_policy, transient_retry_stream) — confirmed above. IMPORTANT.

2. **Missing parent-dir creation → silent no-op on fresh homes** — confirmed. Severity decision: IMPORTANT or BLOCKING. The feature silently produces nothing when `~/.fah/logs` doesn't exist. The telemetry sink sibling creates the dir. It self-heals after the first fa.log write. Opt-in diagnostic; no host breakage. Hmm. Per "BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior..." — the feature's behavior is broken in a real environment class, and it's SILENT (the user believes they're tracing). I keep going back and forth. Let me settle: the severity definitions: "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug... Must be fixed." This would cause a bug (silent empty trail) for fresh-home users. The fix is one line. Given "when in doubt, start one level higher", I'll mark it BLOCKING — it's a genuine functional defect of the feature being reviewed, silently degrading its core deliverable. And with verdict mapping: any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES.

Wait — but I should be careful about triggering a rework round for something that self-heals. Let me reconsider once more... The PR description explicitly claims "silent IO failure" handling as reviewed-hardening. The truncation failure is silently swallowed AND the trace keeps "running" (timer, seq) while producing zero bytes. The user-facing contract "one line per mark at ~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log" is void. A diagnostic tool that silently records nothing is broken — not degraded, broken. BLOCKING it is. Both findings (dir creation + wrapper double-emit) are correctness-of-the-feature bugs.

Actually for the double-emit: is it really wrong per the documented contract? The code comment says "one line per delta leaving ANY provider adapter". With wrappers, each delta leaves the inner adapter (1 emit) then leaves the outer wrapper stream (another emit). The doc in stream_trace.dart says `emit` — "a provider adapter pushed a delta event into the [AssistantMessageEventStream]". Both pushes ARE pushes into an AssistantMessageEventStream. So technically "as coded" — but the trail's analytical purpose ("net→emit gap names the adapter/SE-decode cost, emit→render the loop/UI cost") breaks: with 2-3 emit lines per delta, the emit→render gap computation from the log gets ambiguous, and emit lines no longer identify adapter cost. Also `+Nch` duplicated details make chunk counting wrong. It corrupts the diagnostic's core answer. IMPORTANT (not BLOCKING — the feature still functions, data is interpretable with care; no functional bug outside the diagnostic). Hmm, "when in doubt, start one level higher"... The PR's stated purpose is answering "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone. With duplicate emits, every delta shows 2-3 lines; the user CAN still compute (take the LAST emit before each render). It's degraded, not broken. IMPORTANT.

So: 1 BLOCKING (dir creation → silent no-op), 1-2 IMPORTANT (double emit; concurrent-run truncation/clobber), plus suggestions.

3. **Concurrent armed runs clobber**: `fa dap start` spawns `fa hub serve` detached (env inherited → armed → truncates parent's trail). Also two terminals. The path is fixed. Severity: the hub-serve child truncation happens at spawn — but does `fa hub serve` itself reach the StreamTrace install? It goes through main() → _runApp → `if (args.first == 'hub') exit(await runHubCommand(...))` — the install in main() happens BEFORE that interception (line ~88, interception at fah_runapp line 39). So yes, hub serve truncates the file at boot when env inherited. Is FA_STREAM_TRACE inherited? `Process.start`/detached spawn inherit the parent env by default. So `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa dap start` (or `fa serve` spawning?) destroys the parent's trail. Also `fa serve --a2a` is long-running; a second terminal REPL truncates its trail. Real footgun in the primary workflow (diagnosing a live serve). Severity: SUGESTION or IMPORTANT? The design doc acknowledges "ONE trace per file — collect across runs by copying the file between runs" — the author chose truncation knowingly. The hub-child inheritance is a subtler instance of the same choice. I'll make this a SUGESTION (design was explicit; the consequence is confined to the opt-in diagnostic) — but mention the detached-hub-child inheritance as the concrete scenario making it worse than "copy between runs" implies. Hmm, actually — think again: who runs `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa` AND ALSO spawns hub serve from that same session? `fa dap start` is a user action inside the REPL? No — `fa dap start` is a CLI subcommand, run from a shell. If the user's shell profile exports FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 permanently, then EVERY fa invocation truncates the trail of every concurrently-running fa — including the `fa hub serve` daemon at boot... wait no, hub serve truncates when IT boots (already running daemon doesn't re-truncate). Scenario: profile exports the var. User runs `fa serve --a2a` (long-lived, armed, trail A). User starts `fa dap start` → spawns `fa hub serve` → truncates trail A mid-diagnosis, then the hub daemon (which never streams) owns the file; serve's subsequent lines append (both append, interleaved). Trail A pre-dap is gone. Real but niche and self-inflicted (persistent env export). SUGESTION.

4. **`net` mark fires per raw HTTP chunk — includes non-SE bodies?** createSseIterator is only used for SSE streaming. Fine.

5. **`render` mark only in TUI CliIO**: headless runs have no render lines; the doc in stream_trace.dart describes render as "the host wrote the delta to its live surface (the CLI's `_TuiCliIO.write`)" — accurate for the CLI. The flutter_app has its own host (not wired) — out of scope, PR says CLI. Fine.

6. **Test pollution**: `StreamTrace.start` is global static. The io test starts traces; tearDown stops. Tests within the same package run in the same process? `dart test` runs each FILE in its own isolate by default (concurrency across files). So global state pollution across files isn't an issue. Fine.

7. **`stream_trace_io_test.dart` env-gate test writes `off-null.log`** etc. — fine.

8. **The 600ms sleep test** — makes the suite slower; acceptable (they kept it to prove the timer). Fine.

9. **Clock: `Stopwatch` measures elapsed; `DateTime.now()` per line for wall-clock prefix — good for cross-referencing fa.log.**

10. **`FileStreamTraceSink.flush` uses `writeAsStringSync` on the hot path every 250ms timer tick when pending non-empty — sync IO on the UI/event-loop thread. Deliberate (documented). Fine.

11. **`buffer threshold check `_pending.length >= _kFlushThresholdBytes`** — StringBuffer.length is UTF-16 code units — fine for a byte-ish threshold.

12. **Line counts**: all new files well under the 280 gate. agent_cli.dart is a part-file host — adding one import; file was already near a gate? Let me check wc -l of agent_cli.dart — the god-file ceiling is 280; the PR adds 1 line. Let me check quickly.

13. **PR description backslash typo**: "CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)" — a stray backslash in pr_info/ticket; cosmetic, in the ticket only, not the code. Skip (or note the doc nit). The in-code docs are clean.

14. **AGENTS.md patterns**: The AGENTS.md says provider forensics seams install at the host boundary via `installProviderStallForensics()` — StreamTrace installs separately in main(); consistent with the pattern (its own io file + lib/io.dart export). Fine.

15. **Security**: no secrets in trace lines (counts only). The file path is under the user's home. Env gate exact-match '1'. No injection surface. Windows path building fine. 

16. **`maybeStartStreamTrace` constructs `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` only after env check — no file I/O unless armed. Good.

17. One more: **the `emit` switch uses `default: break;`** — StartEvent, ToolCallBegin/End etc. produce no emit line. Deliberate (deltas only). Fine.

18. **`DoneEvent() || ErrorEvent()` → 'terminal'** — but `end([result])` (called by wrappers `onDone: outer.end`) closes the controller WITHOUT a push — term…
All neighboring suites pass. Exhaustive pass now — checking remaining details: `_TuiCliIO` usage vs other CliIO implementations, and the god-file gate on `agent_cli.dart`.

So:
- In TUI mode (`useTui && io.supportsRawMode`), `_TuiCliIO` wraps `_TerminalCliIO` — render marks fire.
- In line-mode REPL (no raw mode, e.g. piped input) and headless (`-p`), the raw `_TerminalCliIO` is used directly — **no render marks**. So the trail's `render` mark exists only interactive TUI runs. The PR documents this scope ("the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write`)"), so it's a known scope, not a bug. The diagnostics value for the bursty-endpoint use case (headless bench runs!) is limited though — headless is exactly where you'd diagnose a bursty endpoint, and there render lines are absent. Worth a SUGESTION (wire the mark into the shared write path or document that render requires TUI). Hmm — actually, where does the headless host render deltas? Headless mode captures output and writes at the end (`CliIO.write` = primary stream — headless writes assistant text deltas to stdout? "response on stdout"). `_TerminalCliIO.write` in headless writes deltas to stdout as they arrive. So a headless run COULD have render marks — they're just not wired. SUGESTION.

Also `_TuiCliIO.write` fires for ANY primary-stream write — the composer prompt, banners. In TUI mode the input prompt goes through `write`? "write carries the primary stream (assistant text deltas, the input prompt)". So render lines include non-delta writes (prompt echo). Noise in the trail; the `+Nch` detail can't distinguish. Minor — fold into the emit-pollution SUGESTION or mention in general.

Wait — one more important check on `_TuiCliIO.write` in TUI mode: does the TUI `sendOutput` path get called once per delta, or does the agent loop write bigger batches (e.g. whole markdown blocks)? Doesn't matter for correctness.

Now — the `render` mark in `_TuiCliIO.write` fires when `write` is called by ANYONE (not just streaming deltas): e.g. the assistant message final render, code blocks, banners... For a per-chunk timing trail, extra render lines interleave. Acceptable noise; SUGESTION-worthy only as part of a broader "trail noise" note. I'll fold: double/triple emit lines per delta (wrapper hops) + render lines for non-delta writes + absent render in headless → one IMPORTANT (emit duplication, it corrupts the measurement) + one SUGESTION (render scope).

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `emit` fires once per wrapper hop — each delta produces 2–3 `emit` lines, corrupting the gap the trail exists to measure**

The comment says "one line per delta leaving ANY provider adapter", but `AssistantMessageEventStream.push` is overridden on *every* instance of the class — including the wrapper streams that re-push inner events:

- `transientRetryStreamFunction._drive` → `_runAttempt` forwards every inner event through `out.push(event)` (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`), and `provider_catalog.dart:773` wraps **every** provider call in it ("Every provider call … rides the transient-network retry");
- `streamDial`'s cache-probe wrapper re-pushes every inner event via `outer.push(event)` (`lib/src/providers/dial.dart:161`);
- `silent_stream_policy.dart` `_runAttempt` likewise re-pushes forwarded events through its own `out`.

So on a real run the wire shape per delta is `net` → `emit` (adapter) → `emit` (transient-retry hop, +0–1ms) → [`emit` (DIAL hop)] → `render`. Consequences for the diagnostic itself:

1. the `net→emit` gap no longer names the adapter/SSE-decode cost — the *first* `emit` does, but nothing in the line distinguishes it from the wrapper hops;
2. delta counting from `emit` lines over-counts by the hop factor, so "streamed x ms / N chunks" summaries built from the log are wrong;
3. a ~0ms `emit→emit` pair can be misread as pipeline lag.

Fix options, cheapest first:

- Mark only the innermost stream: e.g. a constructor flag (`AssistantMessageEventStream(traced: false)` for wrapper `out` streams), or
- include the hop in the detail (`'text +N hop:retry'`), or
- at minimum, correct the comment + docs in `stream_trace.dart` to state that each wrapper layer emits its own line, so log readers know to take the *first* emit after each net line.

Whatever shape you pick, a test asserting one `emit` line per delta through `transientRetryStreamFunction`-wrapped streams would pin it.

💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.
