## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1727
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1727
- **Title**: feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 net→emit→render timing trail
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/stream-trace` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +686
- **Deletions**: -52
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T19:23:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T00:35:12Z

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)

- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

- 🚨 `stream_trace_io.dart:30` — missing parent-dir creation; silent empty trail (contrast `FileAgentTelemetrySink.record`, which creates the parent)
- ⚠️ `event_stream.dart:138` — `transientRetryStreamFunction` (wraps every provider call) and the DIAL cache-probe wrapper re-push events, doubling/tripling `emit` lines per delta
- 💡 Fixed-path truncate-on-start clobbers concurrent armed runs (two terminals; `fa dap start`'s detached `fa hub serve` child); `render` mark is TUI-only so headless trails lack the emit→render leg; `start` never releases a replaced sink's timer

**Next Steps**:
1. `File(path).parent.createSync(recursive: true)` (best-effort) before truncating + a fresh-nested-dir test
2. Trace only the innermost stream (or hop-tag the emit lines); pin with a wrapped-stream test
3. Consider pid-qualified/append+header log naming, headless render wiring, and sink release on `start`/`stop`

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fixed path + truncate-on-start lets any concurrently armed `fa` wipe the live trail**

The path is a single fixed file (`~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`) and every armed boot truncates it. Truncate-per-run is a documented choice, but two reachable flows make it lose data you did not consent to lose:

1. Two terminals: `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1 fa serve --a2a` streaming a long diagnosis, then any second armed `fa` invocation (REPL, `fa trajectory tail`, even a quick `fa -p`) truncates the live trail mid-run.
2. Detached children inherit the env: `fa dap start` (run from a shell with the knob exported) spawns `fa hub serve` detached; the child passes through this same install point in `main()` (the install precedes the `hub` subcommand interception), truncating the parent's trail at spawn.

If the single-file design is intentional, consider one of: a pid-qualified filename (`stream-trace-<pid>.log` with the last N retained), or append-mode + a `=== run <pid> <iso> ===` header line so concurrent runs interleave but never destroy each other. At minimum, document the concurrent-run caveat next to the "collect across runs by copying the file between runs" note.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `render` mark exists only in the TUI seam — headless runs (the natural bench for a bursty endpoint) record no render leg**

`_TuiCliIO.write` is only installed when `useTui && io.supportsRawMode` (`agent_cli.dart:362`); headless (`fa -p`) and line-mode REPL run on the raw `_TerminalCliIO`, so their trails contain `net`/`emit` only and the emit→render gap — the number this PR's description leads with — is unmeasurable precisely in the scripted/bench runs where you'd most likely chase a bursty endpoint.

Also note `write` carries more than deltas in TUI mode (the input prompt echo and other primary-stream writes hit the same seam), so `render` lines are a superset of rendered deltas.

Consider wiring the same one-line mark into the headless write path (or into a shared `CliIO` decorator), and/or naming the TUI-only scope in the `stream_trace.dart` docs so a missing `render` leg in headless logs reads as scope, not as a bug.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

## Review Summary — PR #1727 (StreamTrace diagnostic)

**Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES`** (1 blocking correctness bug, 1 important, 3 suggestions)

**Findings:**
1. 🚨 **BLOCKING** (`stream_trace_io.dart:30`) — `FileStreamTraceSink` never creates `~/.fah/logs/`; `bin/fah.dart` arms the trace before anything creates that dir, and every IO failure is swallowed — so on fresh installs, fresh `$HOME`s, and ephemeral bench containers an armed (`FA_STREAM_TRACE=1`) trace silently records nothing. The sibling `FileAgentTelemetrySink` establishes the create-parent-dir pattern the sink should follow.
2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`event_stream.dart:138`) — the `emit` mark in the `push` override fires once per **wrapper hop**: `transientRetryStreamFunction` (wraps *every* provider call per `provider_catalog.dart:773`) and DIAL's cache-probe wrapper re-push inner events, so each delta logs 2–3 `emit` lines and corrupts the net→emit gap the trail exists to measure.
3. 💡 Fixed-path truncate-on-start clobbers concurrent armed runs (incl. the detached `fa hub serve` child spawned by `fa dap start`, which inherits the env and passes the same install point); `render` is TUI-only so headless trails lack the emit→render leg; `StreamTrace.start` never releases a replaced sink's timer.

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. ## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

3. 💡 Fixed-path truncate-on-start clobbers concurrent armed runs (incl. the detached `fa hub serve` child spawned by `fa dap start`, which inherits the env and passes the same install point); `render` is TUI-only so headless trails lack the emit→render leg; `StreamTrace.start` never releases a replaced sink's timer.

## PR Description

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

## Files

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart` (file sink + env-gated installer, `lib/io.dart` only)
- wiring: `bin/fah.dart` (install), `event_stream.dart` (`push` override = emit), `provider_common.dart` (net), `agent_cli_io.dart` (render)

## Tests

- `test/providers/stream_trace_test.dart` — pure contract (marks, ordering, stop-drops-late-marks)
- `test/providers/stream_trace_io_test.dart` — buffering, truncation, silent IO failure, env gate

## What

Opt-in per-chunk timing trail for the streaming pipeline, split out of the goal_builder resume PR (#1726) per review (that PR ships fixes only; this one is the diagnostic feature).

Three marks, one line each at `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log`:

- `net` — raw bytes arrived from the provider socket (the `createSseIterator` read leg)
- `emit` — a provider adapter pushed a delta into `AssistantMessageEventStream`
- `render` — the host wrote the delta to its live surface (CLI `_TuiCliIO.write\)

Every line carries `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>` — comparing a `net` line with the `emit`/`render` lines that follow answers "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone (bursty endpoint cadence vs render-pipeline lag).

Armed by `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` (exactly `1`) at `fa` boot; OFF by default; pure Dart (`stream_trace.dart`, barrel-exported), dart:io sink behind `lib/io.dart`. Review hardening already folded in:

- **Buffered flush** — lines flush on a 250ms timer / 64KB threshold / `dispose()`; no sync fsync per SSE chunk on the hot path (a per-chunk flush perturbed the cadence being measured)
- **Windows** — arms under `USERPROFILE` too (`HOME` is unset there), same fallback as `_homeDir()`
- **Docs** — real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]` (no `.lookup` member exists); the sink truncates on start (one trail per run)

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` (pure: marks, line format, active-trace lifecycle)
